comment: The missed comparisons were A over E and D over C. A’s deeper normalized residual rectifier overcame E’s roughly 10× nominal Adagrad displacement; I overextended K1012’s progress preference and underweighted K1074. D’s zero-LN LeakyReLU beat C’s normalized residual SiLU, so K1006’s LN preference was too strong here; K1008 flags the rectifier advantage but does not settle unequal LN counts. Backtests: rectifiers with one fewer LN won 4/5 low-rate Adam history pairs and 2/2 lab pairs, with architecture confounded. Deep normalized Adagrad beat faster shallow rivals in 2/2 history pairs from one question, but only 2/6 lab pairs across five sets. These results do not establish a general mechanism or reliable combined rule.
